Lesko?Help

Free Cars & Transportation Help
Need a vehicle or a way to get to work, school, or medical care? Charities donate cars to families in
need, and other programs help with rides and fares. Below are the main national starting points. Tick
the box once you’ve contacted each one.

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

There are real charities that give away donated cars — but demand is high and applying is always free.
Be patient and apply to several. Any program charging an application fee is a scam.

1 Charities That Donate Cars

These national nonprofits refurbish donated vehicles and give them to qualifying families, often for work or
medical need.

Free Charity Cars / 1-800-Charity Cars
The nation’s oldest and largest car-donation charity. Apply online; priority for survivors, veterans, and
families with urgent need.
→ www.800charitycars.org

Working Cars for Working Families (NCLC)
A national directory of car-ownership programs — the best tool to find a local group that gives or finances
cars near you.
→ www.workingcarsforworkingfamilies.org

Vehicles for Change
Provides low-cost cars to working families in the areas it serves, and runs auto-training programs.
→ www.vehiclesforchange.org

2 Help Through Local Programs

State and local programs sometimes provide cars or transportation help tied to work or job training.

TANF — Work-Related Transportation
If you get TANF (cash assistance), your state may help with a car, repairs, or transport to work. Ask your
caseworker.
→ www.acf.hhs.gov/ofa/programs/tanf/about

211 — Local Vehicle & Ride Help
Call or search for local car-donation programs, gas cards, and transportation help.
→ www.211.org or dial 211

 3 Get to Medical Care

If your need is getting to doctor visits, there’s free non-emergency medical transportation for many people.

Medicaid Non-Emergency Medical Transportation
If you have Medicaid, you may get free rides to medical appointments. Ask your state Medicaid office or
plan.
→ www.medicaid.gov/medicaid/benefits/non-emergency-medical-transportation

Eldercare Locator — Senior Rides
Connects older adults to local transportation services and ride programs.
→ eldercare.acl.gov or call 1-800-677-1110

4 Everyday Ride Help

For getting to work or job interviews while you wait for a car.

Local Public Transit Reduced Fares
Most transit agencies offer reduced fares for seniors, people with disabilities, and low-income riders. Ask
your local transit office.
→ Ask your local transit agency

United Way / Ride United
In many areas, United Way partners on rides to work, interviews, and appointments. Ask 211.
→ www.211.org or dial 211

⚠ WATC H O U T F O R

★ A T I P T H AT H E L P S

If a “free car” offer asks for a fee, gift card, or your
bank login to “release” the vehicle, it’s a scam. Real
charities never charge to apply and never ask for
payment to hand over a car.

Apply to more than one car charity and keep your
application updated — waitlists are long and need is
weighed heavily. A short letter explaining how a car
gets you to work can make your case stronger.

Q U I C K G U I D E · C A R S & C A R R E PA I R S

Lesko?Help

Car Repair & Vehicle Help
A broken-down car can mean a lost job. There’s no single national “car repair grant,” but charities,
community agencies, and free recall repairs can get you back on the road. Below are the main national
starting points. Tick the box once you’ve contacted each one.

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

Real car-repair help is free to apply for. Any website or caller charging a “registration” or “processing”
fee to submit your application is a scam. Always get a written repair estimate from a licensed mechanic
before applying.

1 Start Local — Fastest Help

Local agencies and 211 are usually the quickest route to repair help, gas cards, or a referral.

211 — Local Car Repair Help
Call or search to find local repair assistance, nonprofit garages, and emergency transportation help.
→ www.211.org or dial 211

Community Action Agency — Find Yours
Local agencies may help with car repairs or transportation so you can keep working. Ask what’s available.
→ communityactionpartnership.com/find-a-cap

2 Charities That Repair Cars

National nonprofits repair cars or partner with local mechanics for free or discounted work, usually for
working families.

Working Cars for Working Families (NCLC)
Publishes a national list of car-ownership and repair programs by area. The best place to find a local
program.
→ www.workingcarsforworkingfamilies.org

Free Charity Cars / 1-800-Charity Cars
The nation’s oldest vehicle charity — also helps with essential repairs to make a car safe. Priority for
domestic-abuse survivors, military families, and medical need.
→ www.800charitycars.org

Catholic Charities & St. Vincent de Paul
Many local chapters help with car repairs or payments for working families. Call your local office.
→ www.catholiccharitiesusa.org/find-help

3 Free Safety-Recall Repairs

If your car has an open safety recall, the manufacturer must fix it for free — no income limit, any car owner.

NHTSA — Check for Recalls
Enter your license plate or VIN to see open recalls. Recall repairs are always free at a dealer.
→ www.nhtsa.gov/recalls

Lesko Help

Cars & Car Repairs · Car Repair & Vehicle Help

Page 1 of 2

 4 Faith & Community Garages

Some churches and nonprofit garages do free or deeply discounted repairs for people who need a car for
work.

Local Church “Car Care” Ministries
Many churches run benevolence or car-care ministries. Call local churches or ask 211 for one near you.
→ Ask 211 or local churches

Nonprofit Repair Garages
Some areas have garages offering 50–80% off for low-income workers. Search your city + “nonprofit auto
repair.”
→ Search your city + 'nonprofit auto repair'

⚠ WATC H O U T F O R

★ A T I P T H AT H E L P S

Government car-repair help is a top target for
scams. Never pay a fee to apply, and don’t trust a
caller who “guarantees” a repair grant. Real programs
are free and ask for proof of income and need.

Get a written, itemized estimate from a licensed
mechanic first — most programs require it, and it
helps you avoid being overcharged. Explain you need
the car for work; many programs prioritize
employment.

Q U I C K G U I D E · H O M E & H O U S I N G H E L P

Foreclosure Help & Homes for $1
Struggling with your mortgage, or hoping to buy a very low-cost home? There’s free help to avoid
foreclosure, plus real government programs that sell homes cheaply. Below are the main national
starting points. Tick the box once you’ve contacted each one.

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

Free foreclosure help exists — never pay a company that “guarantees” it can save your home for an
upfront fee. The safest first call is a HUD-approved housing counselor, who helps you for free.

1

Free Foreclosure-Prevention Help

If you’re behind on your mortgage, a free HUD counselor can contact your lender, explain your options, and
help you apply for relief.

HUD-Approved Housing Counselor
Free expert help to avoid foreclosure and deal with your lender. Find one near you.
→ www.hud.gov/findacounselor

HUD Foreclosure Help Line
Call to reach a free local foreclosure-prevention counselor.
→ 1-800-569-4287

CFPB — Mortgage & Housing Help
Official tool for mortgage relief options and avoiding foreclosure scams.
→ www.consumerfinance.gov/coronavirus/mortgage-and-housing-assistance

2 Help Paying Your Mortgage

Some state programs still help homeowners who’ve fallen behind. Funds are limited, so check your state.

State Homeowner Assistance Fund (HAF)
Some states still have mortgage-relief funds for homeowners who fell behind. Check your state’s program
through a HUD counselor or your state HFA.
→ www.ncsha.org/homeowner-assistance-fund

3 Buy a Home Cheaply — Government Sales

Government agencies sell foreclosed and surplus homes, sometimes far below market price.

HUD Homes for Sale
Homes HUD has taken back, often priced below market. Browse by state.
→ www.hudhomestore.gov

Good Neighbor Next Door — 50% Off
Teachers, police, firefighters, and EMTs can buy eligible HUD homes at half price (live there 3 years).
→ www.hud.gov/program_offices/housing/sfh/reo/goodn/gnndabot

USDA Homes for Sale
Foreclosed rural homes sold by USDA, sometimes with low-down-payment financing.
→ www.resales.usda.gov

Lesko Help

Home & Housing Help · Foreclosure & $1 Homes

Page 1 of 2

 4 The Truth About “Homes for $1”

You may have heard of $1 homes. They’re real but limited — here’s where they actually come from.

HUD Dollar Homes Program
HUD sells some unsold homes to local governments for $1, which then offer them to residents through
local programs. Ask your city/county housing office.
→ www.hud.gov/buying/government/dollarhomes

Local Land Banks
Many cities sell abandoned homes very cheaply to fix up. Search your city plus “land bank” or ask in the
Questions area.
→ Search your city + 'land bank'

⚠ WATC H O U T F O R

★ A T I P T H AT H E L P S

Foreclosure “rescue” scams target struggling
homeowners — never sign over your deed or pay big
upfront fees. The $1 home programs go through local
governments, not random websites charging for a
“list.”

Call a HUD counselor the moment you know you’ll
miss a payment — the earlier you act, the more
options you have. Lenders often have relief programs
they only offer if you reach out.

Lesko?Help

Utility Assistance — Energy & Water
Behind on gas, electric, heating, or water? You may qualify for federal and local programs that help pay
what you owe and keep your service on. Below are the most trusted national starting points. Tick the
box once you’ve contacted each one.

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

Call your utility company first and ask for their hardship program, payment plan, or budget billing — and
tell them if you’ve had a shut-off notice. Then apply to the programs below. A real assistance program
never charges a fee just to apply.

1

Federal Energy Bill Help (LIHEAP)

LIHEAP is the main federal program for heating, cooling, and electricity costs. You apply through your state or
local Community Action Agency.

LIHEAP — Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program
Helps pay heating and cooling bills, and in many states helps during an energy crisis or shut-off. Find your
state’s program and how to apply.
→ www.acf.hhs.gov/ocs/programs/liheap

LIHEAP Help Line
Call to find the office that takes applications in your area.
→ 1-866-674-6327 National Energy Assistance Referral

2 Help With Your Water Bill

The federal water assistance program (LIHWAP) has ended, so water help now comes from your water
company and local agencies. These are the best places to start.

Your Water Company — Hardship & Payment Plans
Most water utilities have low-income discounts, payment plans, or shut-off protection. Call the number
on your bill and ask what they offer.
→ Call the number on your water bill

211 — Local Water & Utility Help
Call or search to find local programs that help with overdue water and utility bills.
→ www.211.org or dial 211

Lesko Help

Pay Debt & Bills · Utility Assistance

Page 1 of 2

 3 Local Hands-On Help

Community agencies and charities help you apply, cover emergency bills, and prevent shut-offs — often for
several utilities at once.

Community Action Agency — Find Yours
Local agencies run LIHEAP and other utility help, and can walk you through applying.
→ communityactionpartnership.com/find-a-cap

Dollar Energy Fund
Works with utility companies to help pay overdue energy and water bills.
→ www.dollarenergy.org

Salvation Army — Utility Assistance
Local branches may help with emergency utility bills. Availability depends on funding.
→ www.salvationarmyusa.org

4 Lower Your Bills For Good (Weatherization)

Free home energy upgrades — insulation, weather-sealing, repairs — that permanently cut your energy bills.
No cost to eligible households.

Weatherization Assistance Program (WAP)
Free energy-saving improvements for income-eligible homes. Find how to apply in your state.
→ www.energy.gov/scep/wap/how-apply-weatherization-assistance

⚠ WATC H O U T F O R

★ A T I P T H AT H E L P S

Old websites still list “LIHWAP” water grants — that
federal program ended and is no longer taking
applications. Use your water company and 211
instead.

Apply before you’re disconnected. Many programs
offer emergency help or can stop a shut-off if you
reach out in time. Funds often run out, so apply early
in the season.

Lesko?Help

Student Loan Help
Federal student loan rules keep changing — but you have real options to lower your payments and, for
many people, get loans forgiven. Everything official is free at StudentAid.gov. Tick the box once you’ve
looked into each one.

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

You never have to pay a company to manage or “forgive” your federal student loans — every application
is free at StudentAid.gov. The SAVE repayment plan ended by court order in 2026, so ignore any site still
promoting it.

1 Start Here — Your Federal Loan Account

StudentAid.gov is the official site for everything: your balance, your servicer, repayment plans, and forgiveness
applications.

StudentAid.gov — Your Dashboard
Log in to see your loans, your servicer, and your options. The starting point for everything below.
→ studentaid.gov

Loan Simulator — Compare Plans
A free tool that estimates your payments under each repayment plan and shows which fits your situation.
→ studentaid.gov/loan-simulator

2 Lower Your Monthly Payment

Income-driven repayment (IDR) sets your payment based on income and family size. After 20–25 years of
payments, the rest may be forgiven.

Income-Driven Repayment (IDR)
Apply for an income-based plan. IBR is the main one being processed right now; a new plan (RAP) is being
added. Apply free.
→ studentaid.gov/manage-loans/repayment/plans/income-driven

Trouble Paying? Deferment & Forbearance
If you can’t pay right now, you may pause payments. Ask your servicer, but know interest may still build
up.
→ studentaid.gov/manage-loans/lower-payments/get-temporary-relief

Lesko Help

Pay Debt & Bills · Student Loan Help

Page 1 of 2

 3 Get Your Loans Forgiven

Several forgiveness programs written into law are still active and discharging loans in 2026.

Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF)
Work full-time for government or a 501(c)(3) nonprofit? Your remaining balance can be forgiven after 120
qualifying payments. Use the PSLF Help Tool.
→ studentaid.gov/pslf

Teacher Loan Forgiveness
Teach 5 years in a low-income school and you may get up to $17,500 forgiven.
→ studentaid.gov/manage-loans/forgiveness-cancellation/teacher

Disability & Closed School Discharge
Loans can be discharged if you have a total and permanent disability, or your school closed. Both still
accept applications.
→ studentaid.gov/manage-loans/forgiveness-cancellation

4 If You’re Behind or in Default

Being behind isn’t the end of the road — there are official ways to get back on track and protect your wages
and tax refund.

Get Out of Default
Options like loan rehabilitation can restore your loan to good standing. Start with your servicer or
StudentAid.gov.
→ studentaid.gov/manage-loans/default/get-out

Free Help & Complaints (FSA Ombudsman)
Free federal help if you’re stuck with your servicer or have a dispute.
→ studentaid.gov/feedback-ombudsman/disputes/prepare

⚠ WATC H O U T F O R

★ A T I P T H AT H E L P S

Never pay a company that promises fast “loan
forgiveness” for a fee — the FTC has shut down
many of these. Everything they offer, you can do
yourself for free at StudentAid.gov. The SAVE plan is
no longer available.

Even if forgiveness feels far off, getting on an
income-driven plan now can drop your payment to
an affordable amount — sometimes very low — and
start your forgiveness clock.

Q U I C K G U I D E · H O M E & H O U S I N G H E L P

Home Repair & Energy Upgrade Grants
Need a new roof, furnace, or critical repair you can’t afford? Federal and local programs offer grants
and very low-interest loans to fix safety hazards and cut your energy bills. Below are the main national
programs. Tick the box once you’ve contacted each one.

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

Grants usually go toward health and safety hazards (roof, heating, plumbing, accessibility) — not
remodels. Seniors, veterans, and people with disabilities often get priority. A real program never charges
a fee just to apply.

1 USDA Repair Help (Rural Homes)

For very-low-income homeowners in rural and many suburban areas. Loans up to $40,000, plus grants for
older homeowners.

USDA Section 504 Home Repair — Loans & Grants
Low-interest (1%) repair loans up to $40,000. Grants up to $10,000 for homeowners age 62+ to remove
safety hazards. Apply through your local Rural Development office.
→ www.rd.usda.gov/programs-services/single-family-housing-programs/single-family-housing-
repair-loans-grants

2 Free Energy Upgrades (Weatherization)

Free improvements — insulation, sealing, sometimes heating repair — that permanently lower your energy
bills. No cost to eligible households.

Weatherization Assistance Program (WAP)
Free energy-saving upgrades for income-eligible homes. Priority for seniors, people with disabilities, and
families with young kids.
→ www.energy.gov/scep/wap/how-apply-weatherization-assistance

LIHEAP — Heating/Cooling Repair
In many states LIHEAP can help repair or replace a broken furnace or AC. Ask your local agency.
→ www.acf.hhs.gov/ocs/programs/liheap

3 Local Government Repair Programs

Cities and counties run their own owner-occupied repair and rehab programs using federal HUD funds.

HUD HOME & CDBG — Local Rehab Programs
Many local governments offer home-repair grants funded by HUD. Ask your city/county housing
department, or a HUD counselor.
→ www.hud.gov/findacounselor

211 — Local Repair Help
Call or search to find repair grants and programs in your area.
→ www.211.org or dial 211

Lesko Help

Home & Housing Help · Home Repair & Energy Grants

Page 1 of 2

 4 Volunteer & Nonprofit Repair

Charities repair and rebuild homes for free or very low cost, especially for seniors, veterans, and people with
disabilities.

Rebuilding Together
Free critical home repairs and accessibility work for low-income homeowners. Find your local affiliate.
→ rebuildingtogether.org

Habitat for Humanity — Home Repair
Many Habitat affiliates offer affordable home repair and weatherization, not just new homes.
→ www.habitat.org/housing-help

VA HISA Grants — Veterans
Home modification grants for veterans with service-connected disabilities (ramps, bathroom safety,
accessibility).
→ www.va.gov/housing-assistance/disability-housing-grants

⚠ WATC H O U T F O R

★ A T I P T H AT H E L P S

Watch out for contractors who push you to take a
loan or sign over a grant they’ll “handle” for you.
Apply directly through USDA, your state, or a trusted
nonprofit — and never pay a fee just to apply.

Get more than one repair estimate from licensed
contractors if a program asks for it. If you need both
a repair and an accessibility change, apply for them
together — a doctor’s or therapist’s note can
strengthen your case.

Q U I C K G U I D E · PAY D E B T & B I L L S

Lesko?Help

Phone, Internet & Devices
Staying connected shouldn’t break the bank. There are federal and nonprofit programs that lower the
cost of phone and internet service, and help you get an affordable computer or tablet. Tick the box
once you’ve contacted each one.

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

The Affordable Connectivity Program (ACP) ended in 2024 — ignore any site still advertising its $30
internet credit. The programs below are the ones that actually work in 2026. A real program never
charges a fee just to apply.

1

Lower Your Phone or Internet Bill (Lifeline)

Lifeline is the main federal program. It gives a monthly discount on phone OR internet service through
participating providers.

Lifeline — Federal Phone & Internet Discount
Up to $9.25/month off phone or internet (up to $34.25 on Tribal lands). Qualify if your income is at or
below 135% of the federal poverty guidelines, or you get SNAP, Medicaid, SSI, or certain other benefits.
→ www.lifelinesupport.org

Lifeline Survivor Benefit (Safe Connections Act)
Survivors of domestic violence or trafficking can get up to 6 months of emergency Lifeline support and
separate a phone line from an abuser’s plan.
→ www.lifelinesupport.org/survivor-benefit

2 Free or Low-Cost Phones

Some Lifeline providers include a free phone with the monthly service discount.

Lifeline Provider Search
Find companies in your state that offer Lifeline — many include a free or very low-cost phone.
→ www.lifelinesupport.org/companies-near-me

SafeLink & Assurance Wireless
Two of the largest Lifeline phone providers. Check eligibility and what device they offer.
→ www.safelink.com

3 Affordable Internet Plans

Many internet providers run their own low-income plans, often around $10–$30/month, separate from any
federal program.

Provider Low-Income Plans
Ask your internet company about their low-income plan. Common ones include Xfinity Internet Essentials,
Spectrum, and AT&T Access.
→ Ask your internet provider directly

EveryoneOn — Find Low-Cost Internet
Enter your ZIP code to find affordable internet offers and devices in your area.
→ www.everyoneon.org

Page 1 of 2

 4 Low-Cost Computers & Tablets

Nonprofits refurbish computers and sell them cheaply to people who qualify.

PCs for People
Low-cost refurbished computers and low-cost internet for income-eligible people.
→ www.pcsforpeople.org

Computers with Causes
Donated computers for people and families in need.
→ www.computerswithcauses.org

Human-I-T
Affordable devices and internet for low-income households.
→ www.human-i-t.org

⚠ WATC H O U T F O R

★ A T I P T H AT H E L P S

Skip any ad still promising the $30 “ACP” or
“Emergency Broadband” internet credit — that
program ended in 2024. Lifeline is the real, active
program now.

You can usually only get one Lifeline discount per
household, and you choose phone or internet. Pair it
with a provider’s own low-income plan to save the
most.

Lesko?Help

Government Auctions & Surplus
The government sells cars, property, and seized goods to the public — often well below retail — and
holds billions in unclaimed money. Below are the official national sites. Tick the box once you’ve
checked each one.

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

Use only official .gov sites and their named partners. Items sell “as-is,” so read every listing carefully and
never pay a separate “membership” site for access to lists you can get free. Checking for unclaimed
money is always free.

1 Start Here — The Official Hub

USA.gov links to every legitimate federal auction and sale in one place.

USA.gov — Auctions & Sales
The official starting point for government auctions of cars, property, and seized goods.
→ www.usa.gov/auctions-and-sales

2 Buy Cars & Surplus Goods

Federal agencies sell vehicles, electronics, equipment, and more to the public.

GSA Auctions
The main federal site for surplus cars, trucks, equipment, and goods from government agencies.
→ www.gsaauctions.gov

GSA Fleet Vehicle Sales
The largest source of used government vehicles — tens of thousands of cars and trucks sold each year.
→ autoauctions.gsa.gov

GovDeals & Public Surplus
Where most state and local agencies (police, schools, transit) sell vehicles and equipment.
→ www.govdeals.com

3 Seized & Forfeited Property

Property seized by federal agencies is sold to the public, including cars, jewelry, and sometimes real estate.

U.S. Marshals Service Auctions
Assets seized in federal cases — vehicles, real estate, and luxury goods.
→ www.usmarshals.gov/assets/sales

U.S. Treasury Auctions
Property forfeited for tax or other violations, sold to the public.
→ www.usa.gov/auctions-and-sales

Food & Grocery Help
If your income doesn’t cover groceries every month, you’re not alone — and real help exists. Federal
benefits and community food programs can put food on your table this week and every month. Tick
the box once you’ve contacted each one.

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

Many people who qualify never apply because they don’t know these programs exist. There’s no risk in
checking your eligibility, and applying is always free. Your local food bank can even help you fill out the
forms.

1 Monthly Grocery Benefits (SNAP)

SNAP (formerly food stamps) loads money onto a card you use like debit at grocery stores and many farmers
markets. It’s the biggest food program in the country.

SNAP — How to Apply
Apply through your state. Income limit is generally around 130% of the federal poverty level, with higher
limits for households with seniors or disabled members.
→ www.fns.usda.gov/snap/recipient/eligibility

Find Your State SNAP Office
Each state runs its own application. This finds your state’s office and online application.
→ www.fns.usda.gov/snap/state-directory

2 Food Right Now (Food Banks & Pantries)

Food banks give out free groceries — shelf-stable items, fresh produce, dairy, sometimes meat. Most serve
anyone in their community who asks.

Feeding America — Find Your Food Bank
A network of 200+ food banks and 60,000 pantries and meal programs. Enter your ZIP to find free food
near you.
→ www.feedingamerica.org/find-your-local-foodbank

211 — Local Food Help
Call or search to find pantries, hot meals, and food programs in your area.
→ www.211.org or dial 211

3 For Pregnant Women, Babies & Young Kids (WIC)

WIC provides healthy foods, formula, nutrition help, and breastfeeding support for families with young
children.

WIC — Women, Infants & Children
Free healthy groceries and support if you’re pregnant, recently had a baby, or have a child under 5, and
meet income rules (or get SNAP, Medicaid, or TANF).
→ www.fns.usda.gov/wic

 4 Help for Kids & Seniors

Targeted programs feed children during the school year and summer, and provide groceries for older adults.

Free & Reduced-Price School Meals

Senior Food Programs

on benefits to use them, and you can use them while

until the cupboard is empty.

Debt Help & Credit Counseling
Drowning in credit card or other debt? Free, trustworthy nonprofit counselors can help you build a
plan, lower your interest, and deal with creditors — without the traps of for-profit “debt relief”
companies. Tick the box once you’ve contacted each one.

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

Real nonprofit credit counseling is low-cost or free and never charges large upfront fees. Be very careful
with companies that promise to “erase” your debt, guarantee results, or tell you to stop paying your
creditors — those are the classic signs of a scam.

1

Free Nonprofit Credit Counseling

Certified counselors review your full situation for free and help you choose a path. Look for the NFCC network
— member agencies don’t charge upfront fees.

NFCC — National Foundation for Credit Counseling
The nation’s largest nonprofit credit counseling network. Connect with a certified counselor who works
with you and your lenders.
→ www.nfcc.org

Find an NFCC Member Agency
Search for a vetted nonprofit counseling agency near you or by phone.
→ www.nfcc.org/agency-finder

2 Lower Your Payments (Debt Management Plan)

A counselor may set up a Debt Management Plan (DMP) — one monthly payment, often with lower interest
rates negotiated with your creditors.

Ask About a Debt Management Plan
Through an NFCC counselor, a DMP can roll your debts into one affordable payment and may lower your
interest. A safer, cheaper alternative to for-profit debt settlement.
→ Ask your NFCC credit counselor

3 Know Your Rights & Report Problems

Federal agencies protect you from abusive debt collectors and scams — and help you take action.

CFPB — Consumer Financial Protection Bureau
Free help if a debt collector is breaking the rules, plus tools to understand your options. File a complaint
online.
→ www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint

FTC — Report Debt Relief Scams
Report companies that charge upfront fees, guarantee results, or impersonate the government.
→ reportfraud.ftc.gov

Lesko Help

Pay Debt & Bills · Debt Help & Credit Counseling

 4 If You’re Considering Bankruptcy

Sometimes a fresh start is the right move. Initial consultations with attorneys are often free, and required
counseling is low-cost.

Find Free or Low-Cost Legal Help
Legal aid offices can advise on bankruptcy and debt. Start here to find help in your area.
→ www.lawhelp.org

Approved Credit Counseling for Bankruptcy
The required pre-bankruptcy counseling must come from a government-approved agency. Use the
official list.
→ www.justice.gov/ust/list-credit-counseling-agencies-approved-pursuant-11-usc-111

★ A T I P T H AT H E L P S

If a company asks for a big fee before doing
anything, “guarantees” it can wipe out your debt, or
tells you to stop paying and stop talking to creditors
— walk away. The FTC shut down a $100M debt scam
in 2025 that did exactly this.

Start with a free NFCC counseling session before
signing anything. A good counselor will lay out all
your options — including ones that cost you nothing
— with no pressure to enroll.

Buying a Home — Grants & Programs
Think you can’t afford to buy? Government-backed loans and down-payment help make
homeownership possible with little or even no money down. Below are the main national programs.
Tick the box once you’ve looked into each one.

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

There is no single national “free house” grant — real help is a stack of low-down-payment loans, state
grants, and tax credits you combine. Legitimate programs never charge a fee just to apply, and a HUD-
approved counselor will guide you for free.

1

Low- & No-Down-Payment Loans

These federal loan programs let you buy with little or nothing down, with easier credit rules than regular
mortgages.

FHA Loans
As little as 3.5% down with flexible credit. The most common first-time buyer loan. Offered by approved
lenders.
→ www.hud.gov/buying/loans

USDA Rural Loans
Zero down payment for homes in eligible rural and many suburban areas. Check the address on the
eligibility map.
→ www.rd.usda.gov/programs-services/single-family-housing-programs

VA Loans — Veterans & Service Members
Zero down, no ongoing mortgage insurance, for eligible veterans, service members, and some surviving
spouses.
→ www.va.gov/housing-assistance/home-loans

2 Down Payment & Closing Cost Help

Every state runs a Housing Finance Agency offering grants and forgivable loans — often $5,000–$15,000+ —
for first-time buyers.

Find Your State Housing Finance Agency
Each state offers first-time buyer grants, low-interest loans, and closing-cost help. Find yours here.
→ www.ncsha.org/housing-help

HUD — Local Homebuying Programs
HUD’s state-by-state list of down-payment assistance and homebuying programs.
→ www.hud.gov/buying/local-buying-programs

Good Neighbor Next Door

areas (live there 3 years).
→ www.hud.gov/program_offices/housing/sfh/reo/goodn/gnndabot

HUD Homes for Sale

Rent & Eviction Help
Behind on rent or facing eviction? Acting fast matters — free legal help and local rental assistance can
keep you housed. Below are the most trusted national starting points. Tick the box once you’ve

If you have a court date, get legal help right away.

1

Find Local Rental Assistance

Federal money now flows through state and local programs. These official tools point you to what’s open near
you.

CFPB — Find Rental Assistance Near You
The official government tool that lists rental and utility assistance programs by state, county, and city.
→ www.consumerfinance.gov/coronavirus/mortgage-and-housing-assistance/renter-protections/
find-help-with-rent-and-utilities

aid below.
→ www.lawhelp.org

→ www.lsc.gov/about-lsc/what-legal-aid/get-legal-help

Free, expert counselors help you understand your options, contact your landlord, and find assistance — at no

Stress & Mental Health
Feeling overwhelmed, anxious, or down? Support is available — from free counseling to low-cost
therapy and self-help tools. You don’t need to be in crisis to ask for help. Below are trusted national
starting points.

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

If you’re in crisis right now, call or text 988. Otherwise, the resources below help you find ongoing,
affordable mental health support. Most health insurance and Medicaid cover mental health care.

1

Find Affordable Therapy & Counseling

Free and low-cost mental health care exists — including sliding-scale clinics that charge based on income.

FindSupport.gov
A government guide to finding the right mental health support and understanding your options.
→ www.findsupport.gov

FindTreatment.gov
Search for low-cost and sliding-scale mental health and substance-use providers near you.
→ www.findtreatment.gov

Community Mental Health Centers (SAMHSA)

Peer support from people who understand — free and available across the country and online.

→ www.nami.org/help 1-800-950-6264

→ www.mhanational.org/finding-help

Trusted, no-cost tools for managing stress, anxiety, and low mood between appointments.

Healthy Food on a Budget
Eating well shouldn’t be a luxury. Federal programs, fresh-produce incentives, and nutrition help make
healthy food more affordable. Below are trusted national starting points. Tick the box once you’ve
looked into each one.

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

Many of these programs stretch your food budget toward fresh, healthy choices — and you may qualify
even if you’re working. Applying is always free.

1 Get Help Buying Groceries

Federal benefits put money toward food each month — the foundation of eating well on a budget.

SNAP — Monthly Grocery Benefits
Money on a card for groceries, including fruits, vegetables, and healthy staples. Apply through your state.
→ www.fns.usda.gov/snap/recipient/eligibility

WIC — Pregnant Women & Young Kids
Free healthy foods, formula, and nutrition support for families with children under 5.
→ www.fns.usda.gov/wic

2 Double Your Money on Fresh Produce

Programs that match your SNAP dollars when you buy fruits and vegetables.

SNAP at Farmers Markets & Double Up
Many markets double your SNAP spending on fresh produce. Find participating markets and Double Up
Food Bucks programs.
→ www.fns.usda.gov/snap/farmers-markets

GusNIP Produce Incentives
Federal produce-incentive programs that stretch your fruit and vegetable budget. Find local programs.
→ www.nifa.usda.gov/grants/programs/hunger-food-security-programs/gus-schumacher-nutrition-

Real, affordable nutrition comes from whole foods —

24/7 Crisis Help
If you or someone you love is in crisis, help is free, confidential, and available right now — any hour, any
day. You don’t have to be suicidal to reach out. Below are the trusted national lifelines. You are not
alone.

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

If someone is in immediate physical danger, call 911. For emotional crises, the lines below are free,
confidential, and open 24/7. You can call, text, or chat — whatever feels easier.

1 Talk to Someone Now

Trained counselors are ready 24/7 for any kind of emotional crisis — not only suicide.

988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
Call or text 988, or chat online, any time. Free, confidential support for any mental health, suicide, or
substance-use crisis.
→ 988lifeline.org call or text 988

Crisis Text Line
Text HOME to 741741 to reach a trained crisis counselor by text, 24/7.
→ www.crisistextline.org text HOME to 741741

2 Specialized Crisis Lines

Dedicated support for veterans, young people, and survivors.

Veterans Crisis Line
Dial 988 then press 1, text 838255, or chat online. Many responders are veterans themselves.
→ www.veteranscrisisline.net 988 then press 1

The Trevor Project (LGBTQ+ Youth)
24/7 crisis support for LGBTQ+ young people. Call, text, or chat.
→ www.thetrevorproject.org/get-help 1-866-488-7386

National DV Hotline
24/7 confidential support for anyone affected by domestic violence.
→ www.thehotline.org 1-800-799-7233

3 Substance Use & Disaster Distress

Free, confidential help for addiction crises and disaster-related distress.

SAMHSA National Helpline
Free, confidential, 24/7 treatment referral and information for mental health and substance use.
→ www.samhsa.gov/find-help/national-helpline 1-800-662-HELP (4357)

Disaster Distress Helpline
24/7 crisis counseling for emotional distress after a natural or human-caused disaster.
→ www.samhsa.gov/find-help/disaster-distress-helpline 1-800-985-5990

Save 988 in your phone now, before you need it —

strength, not weakness.

Brain & Neuro Support
Facing Alzheimer’s, dementia, Parkinson’s, a stroke, MS, or a brain injury — for yourself or a loved one?
National organizations offer free helplines, support groups, and guidance. Below are trusted starting

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

These conditions affect the whole family. The organizations below offer free 24/7 helplines, care
planning, and support groups — you don’t have to figure it out alone. Many also help you find financial
aid.

1 Memory Loss, Alzheimer’s & Dementia

Free 24/7 helplines and care navigation for families facing memory loss.

Alzheimer’s Association
Free 24/7 helpline, care planning, and local support groups for all dementias.
→ www.alz.org/help-support 1-800-272-3900

Eldercare Locator
Connects families to local services, respite care, and support for older adults.
→ eldercare.acl.gov 1-800-677-1110

2 Parkinson’s, MS & Other Conditions

Disease-specific nonprofits with free helplines, education, and local resources.

Parkinson’s Foundation Helpline
Free help understanding Parkinson’s, treatment, and local resources.
→ www.parkinson.org/resources-support 1-800-473-4636

National MS Society
Free support, programs, and financial-help navigation for multiple sclerosis.
→ www.nationalmssociety.org 1-800-344-4867

Brain Injury Association
Free information and a national help line for traumatic brain injury (TBI).
→ www.biausa.org 1-800-444-6443

3 Stroke & Recovery

Support for stroke survivors and their caregivers.

Quit Smoking & Vaping Help
Ready to quit smoking or vaping? Free coaching, free nicotine patches and gum, and proven tools can
double your chances of success. Below are trusted national programs — all free. Tick the box once
you’ve contacted each one.

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

Quitting is hard because nicotine is addictive — not because you lack willpower. Free help works:
coaching plus nicotine replacement doubles your odds. Most insurance and Medicaid cover quit
medicines.

1

Free Quit Coaching & Medicine

State quitlines offer free phone/text coaching and often free starter kits of patches, gum, or lozenges.

1-800-QUIT-NOW
The national quitline connects you to your free state program: a quit coach plus often-free nicotine
patches or gum.
→ www.cdc.gov/tobacco/campaign/tips/quit-smoking 1-800-784-8669

Smokefree.gov
Free quit plans, text-message support, and live help from the National Cancer Institute.
→ smokefree.gov

2 Free Apps & Text Programs

No-cost tools that help you plan, track cravings, and stay quit.

quitSTART App
A free app from Smokefree.gov with tips, craving tools, and progress tracking.
→ smokefree.gov/tools-tips/apps/quitstart

SmokefreeTXT
Free text-message program with daily encouragement and tips. Text QUIT to 47848.
→ smokefree.gov/tools-tips/text-programs text QUIT to 47848

3 Help for Teens & Young People

Free, judgment-free programs designed specifically for young people who vape.

This Is Quitting (Teen Vaping)
A free text program to help teens and young adults quit vaping. Text DITCHVAPE to 88709.
→ truthinitiative.org/thisisquitting text DITCHVAPE to 88709

 4 Special Programs

Targeted free help for veterans and speakers of other languages.

Quit VET — For Veterans

Asian Smokers’ Quitline
Free coaching in Mandarin, Cantonese, Korean, and Vietnamese.

You don’t need to buy expensive programs,
supplements, or special vapes to quit. The proven,
free combination is coaching plus nicotine
replacement — and your quitline provides both.

Pick a quit date and tell someone you trust. Combine
the free coaching with free patches or gum —
people who use both are far more likely to succeed
than those who rely on willpower alone.

Q U I C K G U I D E · H E A LT H C A R E A S S I S TA N C E

Free & Low-Cost Clinics & Health Insurance
No insurance, or can’t afford a doctor? You can still get care. Federal health centers see everyone
regardless of ability to pay, and you may qualify for free or low-cost coverage. Below are trusted
national starting points. Tick the box once you’ve checked each one.

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

Federally funded health centers must see you regardless of insurance or income — you pay on a sliding
scale, sometimes nothing. And many people who think they can’t get insurance actually qualify for free
or low-cost coverage.

1 Get Care Without Insurance

These centers and clinics provide medical, dental, and mental health care on a sliding scale based on income.

HRSA Health Center Finder
Official federal directory of community health centers that must see everyone, regardless of ability to pay.
→ findahealthcenter.hrsa.gov

NeedyMeds — Free Clinics
A national directory of free and low-cost clinics staffed by volunteers.
→ www.needymeds.org/free-clinics

211 — Local Health Help
Call or search for free clinics and health programs in your area.
→ www.211.org or dial 211

2 Get Free or Low-Cost Insurance

You may qualify for free coverage through Medicaid, or low-cost plans with big subsidies through the
marketplace.

Medicaid & CHIP
Free or very low-cost coverage for people with limited income, and for children. Apply any time of year.
→ www.medicaid.gov/about-us/where-can-people-get-help-medicaid-chip/index.html

HealthCare.gov — Marketplace Plans
Compare plans and see if you qualify for subsidies that lower your premium — many people pay very little.
→ www.healthcare.gov

Free Enrollment Help (Navigators)
Free, in-person help understanding and signing up for coverage.
→ localhelp.healthcare.gov

 3 Other Ways to Get Seen

Additional low-cost options for checkups, screenings, and care.

Planned Parenthood
Low-cost reproductive and general health services on a sliding scale.
→ www.plannedparenthood.org

Free Health Screenings
Many health centers and pharmacies offer free blood pressure, diabetes, and cancer screenings. Ask your
local health center.
→ Ask your local health center

⚠ WATC H O U T F O R

★ A T I P T H AT H E L P S

You don’t need to use expensive urgent-care or ER
visits for routine needs. Community health centers
cost far less and offer ongoing care — and
emergency rooms must treat you regardless of
ability to pay.

When you call a health center, ask about their
“sliding fee scale” and bring proof of income — your
visit may cost very little or nothing. Many also have
staff who help you apply for Medicaid on the spot.

Q U I C K G U I D E · H E A LT H C A R E A S S I S TA N C E

Addiction Recovery
Recovery is possible, and help is free and confidential. Whether it’s alcohol, opioids, or other
substances — for you or someone you love — below are trusted national starting points to find
treatment and support.

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

If someone has overdosed or is in danger, call 911. For finding treatment, the SAMHSA helpline below is
free, confidential, and open 24/7. Medicaid and most insurance cover addiction treatment.

1 Get Help Finding Treatment

Free, confidential help to find treatment that fits your situation and budget.

SAMHSA National Helpline
24/7 free, confidential treatment referral and information in English and Spanish.
→ www.samhsa.gov/find-help/national-helpline 1-800-662-HELP (4357)

FindTreatment.gov
Search a national directory of treatment programs, including low-cost and sliding-scale options.
→ www.findtreatment.gov

2 Free Recovery Support Groups

Peer groups offer free, ongoing support — in person and online, nationwide.

Alcoholics Anonymous (AA)
Free meetings worldwide for anyone who wants to stop drinking. Find local and online meetings.
→ www.aa.org

Narcotics Anonymous (NA)
Free peer support meetings for recovery from drug addiction.
→ www.na.org

SMART Recovery
Free, science-based recovery meetings and tools, in person and online.
→ www.smartrecovery.org

Lesko Help

Healthcare Assistance · Addiction Recovery

Page 1 of 2

 3 Prevent Overdose & Support Families

Free naloxone (overdose reversal) and support for families affected by addiction.

Find Free Naloxone (Narcan)

→ nextdistro.org

Al-Anon — For Families
Free support groups for families and friends of people with a drinking problem.
→ al-anon.org

SAMHSA — Find Support
Plain guidance for taking the first steps, for you or a loved one.
→ www.findsupport.gov

Be wary of for-profit “rehab” centers that pressure
you, promise guaranteed cures, or charge huge
upfront fees. Start with the free SAMHSA helpline,
which gives unbiased referrals.

You don’t have to wait until you “hit bottom.” Calling
the helpline costs nothing and they won’t pressure
you — they simply help you understand your options
when you’re ready.

Free & Low-Cost Dental Care
Dental work is expensive and most insurance leaves big gaps — but there is real free and low-cost
care if you know where to look. Below are the most trusted national programs. Tick the box once
you’ve contacted each one.

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

Watch out for advertised “dental grants” that still leave you with a big bill. The programs below are
nonprofits, dental schools, and government services — not sales pitches. A real program never charges a
fee just to apply.

1

Find Free & Low-Cost Clinics Near You

National directories listing community clinics, sliding-scale dentists, and low-cost programs by location.

NeedyMeds — Free & Low-Cost Clinics
A national directory of free and reduced-cost dental clinics. Search by location.
→ www.needymeds.org/free-clinics

Health Center Finder — HRSA
Federally funded health centers offer dental care on a sliding fee scale based on income.
→ findahealthcenter.hrsa.gov

FindHelp.org — Dental Search
Enter your ZIP code and search “dental” for local free or low-cost care.
→ www.findhelp.org

2 Volunteer Dentists Through Dental Lifeline

A national network connecting volunteer dentists with people who qualify — often for free comprehensive
treatment.

Dental Lifeline Network — Donated Dental Services
Free treatment for people who are elderly, have a disability, or are medically fragile. Check your state
program and eligibility.
→ dentallifeline.org/our-state-programs

3 Dental Schools — Low-Cost, Supervised Care

Dental and hygiene schools offer treatment at a fraction of the usual cost, done by students under expert
supervision.

Dental Schools — ADA Directory
Find accredited dental schools that run low-cost clinics open to the public.
→ www.ada.org

Dental Hygiene Programs — ADHA
Hygiene schools offer very low-cost cleanings, X-rays, and preventive care.
→ www.adha.org

 4 Government & Public Coverage

Public programs cover dental care for many adults and children — worth checking even if you think you don’t
qualify.

Medicaid & CHIP Dental Benefits

→ www.medicaid.gov/medicaid/benefits/dental-care

InsureKidsNow — Find a Dentist
A federal tool to find dentists who accept Medicaid and CHIP for children.
→ www.insurekidsnow.gov

Eldercare Locator — For Seniors

→ eldercare.acl.gov or call 1-800-677-1110

5 Special Situations

Targeted programs for children, survivors of violence, and veterans.

America’s ToothFairy — Kids’ Dental Care

→ www.americastoothfairy.org

Give Back a Smile — Survivors of Violence
Free restorative dental care for survivors of domestic and sexual violence.

Call more than one program. Funding and waiting

may say yes. Keep a simple list of who you called and
what they said.

Vision & Hearing Care
Need glasses, an eye exam, or hearing aids but can’t afford them? Nonprofits and programs provide
free or low-cost vision and hearing care. Below are trusted national starting points. Tick the box once

Hearing aids and eye care are expensive, but real help exists — including free eyeglasses and low-cost
hearing aids. Note: many basic hearing aids can now be bought over the counter without an exam.

1

Free & Low-Cost Eye Care

Programs that provide free eye exams and glasses for people who qualify.

EyeCare America
Free eye exams for eligible seniors and those at risk of eye disease, through volunteer ophthalmologists.
→ www.aao.org/eyecare-america

VSP — Eyes of Hope
Free eye exam and glasses gift certificates for people in need.
→ eyesofhope.vsp.com

New Eyes
Helps people get free new eyeglasses through a voucher program.
→ new-eyes.org

2 Low-Cost Glasses

Affordable ways to get glasses if you have a prescription.

Low-Cost Online Eyeglasses
Sites like Zenni and EyeBuyDirect sell glasses from around $10–$20 with your prescription.
→ www.zennioptical.com

Lions Club — Eyeglass Help
Local Lions Clubs collect and provide eyeglasses to people in need. Ask 211 or your local club.
→ Ask 211 or your local Lions Club

 3 Hearing Care & Aids

Free and low-cost help for hearing tests and hearing aids.

Over-the-Counter Hearing Aids

→ www.fda.gov/medical-devices/hearing-aids/otc-hearing-aids-what-you-should-know

Hearing Charities of America
Helps provide hearing aids to people who can’t afford them.

hearing aids — for many people, the new over-the-

Prescription Drug Help
Can’t afford your medications? You may be able to get them free or far cheaper through manufacturer
programs, nonprofits, and discount tools. Below are trusted national starting points. Tick the box once
you’ve checked each one.

⚠ B E F O R E YO U S TA R T

Never skip or split doses to save money before checking these options — many people get the very
same drug free or for a few dollars. Always ask your pharmacist about generics, too.

1

Find Programs for Your Medication

These directories match you to patient-assistance programs based on the exact drug you take.

NeedyMeds
A free database of patient-assistance programs, plus a discount drug card and free-clinic directory.
→ www.needymeds.org

RxAssist
A directory of drug-company programs that give medicines free or cheaply to people who qualify.
→ www.rxassist.org

Medicine Assistance Tool (PhRMA)
Search hundreds of manufacturer assistance programs in one place.
→ medicineassistancetool.org

2 Lower the Price at the Pharmacy

Discount tools and low-cost generics can dramatically cut what you pay, even without insurance.

GoodRx — Compare & Save
Free coupons and price comparisons that can cut prescription costs sharply. No membership needed.
→ www.goodrx.com

Cost Plus Drugs
An online pharmacy selling many generics at very low, transparent prices.
→ costplusdrugs.com

Low-Cost Generic Lists
Many pharmacies sell common generics for about $4. Ask your pharmacy for its discount generic list.
→ Ask your pharmacy

Lesko Help

Healthcare Assistance · Prescription Drug Help

Page 1 of 2

 3 Free Medicine for Those Who Qualify

Nonprofits and clinics provide free medications to low-income and uninsured patients.

SIRUM — Free Surplus Medicine
A nonprofit that redirects unused, unexpired medicine to patients in need.
→ sirum.org/get-medications

Free & Charitable Clinics
Many free clinics include prescription assistance. Find one near you.
→ www.needymeds.org/free-clinics

4 Help for Medicare & Seniors

Special programs lower drug costs for people on Medicare.

Medicare Extra Help (Low-Income Subsidy)
Federal help paying Part D drug costs for people with limited income (up to 150% of poverty level).
→ www.ssa.gov/medicare/part-d-extra-help

State Pharmaceutical Assistance Programs
Some states help residents pay for medications. Ask your SHIP counselor (see the Medicare guide).
→ www.medicare.gov/basics/costs/help/drug-costs

⚠ WATC H O U T F O R

★ A T I P T H AT H E L P S

Avoid websites that charge a “membership” to
access drug discounts — GoodRx and the programs
above are free. And never buy prescription drugs
from unverified overseas sites; they can be unsafe.

Bring the discount price to your pharmacist —
sometimes a coupon beats your insurance copay.
And always ask if a generic version exists; it’s usually
far cheaper and just as effective.
